standard_prerequisites.name: The I-adic completion of a ring as the limit of the quotients R over I^n
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 11769-11773 for part (1)
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the compatible maps D_n on quotients to be assembled into a derivation of the completion.

standard_prerequisites.name: A finite type extension is generated by finitely many elements, and elements of R' are sums of monomials in those generators with coefficients in R
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: used at proof lines 11778-11794 for part (3)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement about all of R' to the finitely many generators, which is the step that makes the power of g sufficient.

core_obligations: Prove (1): use the Leibniz rule to get D(I^n) contained in I^{n-1}, hence induced maps R/I^n to R/I^{n-1}, and pass to the limit to obtain the extension to the completion, the derivation axioms being left to the reader (proof lines 11768-11773).
Prove (2): extend D to the localisation by the explicit formula on fractions and check the axioms (proof lines 11775-11776).

Prove (3): choose generators x_i of R' over R and N with g^N x_i in R, extend g^{N+1}D to R_g by (2), compute g^{N+1}D(x_i) with the Leibniz rule and show it lies in R, then check the defining formula on monomials in the x_i to conclude that g^{N+1}D maps R' into R' (proof lines 11778-11794).

The nearest records are 346 (11859-11910, tag 07PH, a derivation detecting a non-pth-power in a finite-type domain) and 345 (11457-11518, tag 07P4); both use derivations but prove different statements, and public 346 begins about 60 lines after this card's proof ends.
difficulty_reason: The lemma has two easy parts and one hard part: a derivation D of a ring extends canonically to the I-adic completion, extends uniquely to any localisation, and, for a finite type extension R inside R' with R_g isomorphic to R'_g for a nonzerodivisor g of R', some power g^N times D extends to R' (statement lines 11753-11765). The proof is a 28-line argument (proof lines 11768-11795). For (1) it uses the Leibniz rule to see that D maps I^n into I^{n-1}, which gives compatible maps on the quotients R/I^n and hence a limit derivation; the verification of the derivation axioms is explicitly omitted. For (2) it gives the standard formula D(r/s) = D(r)/s - rD(s)/s^2 and leaves the axiom check to the reader. The hard part (3) chooses generators x_i of R' over R, picks N with g^N x_i in R, extends g^{N+1}D first to R_g by (2), computes g^{N+1}D(x_i) by the Leibniz rule, shows the result lies in R' for every generator, and finishes by checking the formula on monomials, which is what turns a statement about generators into a statement about all of R'.
